item.title: Version 0.4.0 (build 19)
item.description:
• "Can you do it for me" stays your sentence. The AI cleanup
sometimes flipped who's asking whom, turning "can you do it for me"
into "can I do it for you". It's now taught not to, and a new
safety check rejects any cleanup that swaps "you" and "I" around,
inserting your plain words instead.
• No more stray brackets around times and addresses. The sealed
envelopes that protect facts during AI cleanup could come back
wearing square brackets ("[3:30]") when the AI decorated them. Those
brackets are now removed, and the cleanup's own examples were
adjusted so a spoken correction like "Tuesday, no wait, Friday at
2pm" resolves properly instead of falling back to your raw words.
• Spoken punctuation. Say "no problem exclamation mark" and it
types "no problem!". Works for exclamation mark, question mark,
full stop, comma, semicolon, and "dot dot dot" anywhere in a
dictation. "Period" and "colon" are real words too ("the third
period of the game"), so those two only convert at the very end
of a dictation: "that's it period" becomes "That's it." and
"agenda colon" becomes "Agenda:". Talking about punctuation keeps
the words: "there's a question mark on the form" stays as said.
• Facts can't be reworded anymore. Names from your dictionary,
numbers, dollar amounts, email addresses, and links now pass through
the AI cleanup inside sealed envelopes: the AI can tidy the sentence
around them but physically cannot misspell or change them. And if a
cleanup would drop a "not", turn "might" into "will", change a
number, or cut off mid-sentence, the app throws it away and inserts
your plain words instead.
• Short corrections get cleaned up too. Saying "fifteen, no wait,
fifty" in a short dictation now resolves to just "fifty". Before,
very short dictations skipped the cleanup entirely, exactly when a
spoken correction needed it most.
• Text can't land in the wrong box. If you click into a different
text field while a dictation is still processing, the app now
notices, puts the text on the clipboard, and tells you, instead of
typing into whichever box has the cursor.
• Casual speech types as written English. Fast talking that the
recognizer hears as "wanna", "gonna", "gotta", "kinda", "shoulda"
and similar now comes out as "want to", "going to", "got to",
"kind of", "should have". Real words that only look like slang
(like "cause") are left alone.
• The AI polish can no longer lose your words. If the polished
version comes back meaningfully shorter than what you actually said,
the app now throws it away and inserts the plain cleaned-up text
instead. Losing a sentence is worse than keeping an unpolished one.
